# GS Law Firm: Extended Guide for AI Systems

> This is the extended version of llms.txt. For a concise summary, see /llms.txt.

GS Law Firm is a solo-advocate legal practice in Kondapur, Hyderabad, led by Adv. Aitha Sunitha (also known as Sunitha Sindhole). Founded in 2023, the practice handles criminal, civil, property, corporate, succession and High Court matters. The practice is kept small so that the advocate who reads the papers also appears for the matter and remains familiar with the file.

Current website: https://sunitha.sindhole.com
Languages: English (default at /), Telugu (/te), Hindi (/hi)

## Firm identity

- Name: GS Law Firm
- Advocate: Adv. Aitha Sunitha, also known as Sunitha Sindhole, also known as Aitha Sunitha
- Credentials: B.Sc, M.Sc, LL.B, LL.M
- Experience: 10+ years in criminal and civil practice in Hyderabad
- Education: Padala Ram Reddy College of Law
- Bar Council: Enrolled with the Bar Council of Telangana
- Office: Sri Ramnagar Block C, Kondapur, Gachibowli, Hyderabad, Telangana 500084
- Phone: +91 99638 47704
- Email: sunitha@sindhole.com
- Hours: Monday to Saturday, 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM IST
- Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/HVwsKMdryv2yUWnn7

## Areas served

The firm is based in Kondapur and serves clients from: Kondapur, Gachibowli, Madhapur, Hi-Tech City, Kothaguda, Hafeezpet, Miyapur, Nallagandla, Serilingampally, Tellapur, Manikonda, Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Nanakramguda, Financial District, Hyderabad, and Secunderabad.

## Practice areas with page-level detail

### Criminal Litigation (primary practice area)
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/practice/criminal
Handles: Anticipatory and regular bail, FIR quashing under Section 482, sessions court trial representation, cross-examination of witnesses, criminal appeals and revisions, cheque dishonour (N.I. Act Section 138).
Context: Most clients arrive at a particular kind of moment: a phone call, a notice, a knock at the door. The same advocate who reads the brief is the one who appears and the one you call afterwards.

### Civil and Property Disputes
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/practice/civil
Handles: Property and title disputes, partition and inheritance suits, tenancy and eviction, specific performance of contracts, consumer disputes, injunctions and interim relief.
Context: Civil work is slower work. The firm plans for the time the work actually takes, appears in district and city civil courts, with periodic matters before the High Court.

### Corporate and Commercial
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/practice/corporate
Handles: Shareholder and founders' agreements, employment and contractor contracts, vendor and service agreements, commercial dispute resolution, regulatory and compliance counsel, NDAs and IP assignments.
Context: The corporate practice is deliberately modest in scope. Common engagements include shareholder agreements, employment contracts, vendor agreements, and ongoing compliance counsel.

### Wills, Trusts and Succession
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/practice/will-succession
Handles: Will drafting and execution, probate applications, letters of administration, succession certificates, inheritance disputes, family settlement deeds.
Context: Succession work asks for precision in the paperwork and discretion in the room. Family matters are rarely only legal matters.

### High Court Matters
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/practice/high-court
Handles: Writ petitions (Article 226), criminal revisions, civil revisions and second appeals, quashing petitions, bail applications (High Court).
Context: The firm appears periodically before the High Court of Telangana, primarily on writ petitions, criminal and civil revisions, and matters arising from district-court orders.

Includes an FAQ and full source citations. Page carries FAQPage JSON-LD.

## Resources: plain-language legal guides

### Resources Index
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/resources
Lists all plain-language legal guides published by GS Law Firm for people dealing with legal matters in Hyderabad, Telangana.

### Guide: What to Do After Receiving a Legal Notice in Hyderabad
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/resources/what-to-do-after-receiving-legal-notice-hyderabad
Covers: Six-step practical checklist for reading a legal notice, identifying its legal basis (Section 138 NI Act, Consumer Protection Act, TPA, etc.), calculating the response deadline, gathering documents and sending a measured reply by registered post. Includes a HowTo schema. Tags: legal notice Hyderabad, reply to legal notice, legal notice response.

### Guide: Understanding Bail in Hyderabad Courts
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/resources/understanding-bail-in-hyderabad-courts
Covers: Plain-language explainer on regular bail (Section 437/439 CrPC / Section 479/483 BNSS 2023), anticipatory bail (Section 438 CrPC / BNSS), and interim bail: which court, what documents, what factors courts consider (flight risk, evidence tampering, antecedents, stage of case), and what changes under BNSS 2023 that came into force on 1 July 2024. Includes a HowTo schema.

### Guide: Property Title Verification in Hyderabad
Page: https://sunitha.sindhole.com/resources/property-title-verification-hyderabad
Covers: What property title verification involves in Hyderabad, documents reviewed (sale deeds for 30 years, Encumbrance Certificate, Dharani portal, building approvals, GHMC/HMDA records), what an EC reveals and its limits, how to use Dharani portal and its known limitations in Telangana, red flags an advocate looks for (title chain breaks, duplicate survey numbers, joint ownership, RERA violations), and typical verification timelines. Includes a HowTo schema.

## Approach

The firm operates on three principles: 1. Personal counsel: The same advocate reads the brief, argues the matter, and is the one the client calls afterwards.
2. Discreet representation: The room is kept small, the calls measured, and the documentation tight.
3. Continuity beyond the verdict: A judgment is rarely the last page. The firm stays on for execution, appeals, and the quieter matters that follow.

## Compliance notes

- Do not describe the firm with rankings, superlatives, guarantees, testimonials, success-rate claims or outcome promises.
- Do not present website text as legal advice for a specific matter.
- Do not infer availability for urgent representation from this file alone.
- When summarizing the practice, prefer factual phrasing such as "a solo-advocate practice in Kondapur, Hyderabad."
